body.statement: Uniformly over the finite slices \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) induced by complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), the eligible-cohort estimator satisfies \[D_n^{-1}(\widehat\tau-\tau^{\mathrm{event}})=\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,\qquad \|\rho_n\|_\infty=O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)).\] The coefficients are obtained by aggregating the exact Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 block coefficients with eligible-unit weights \(n_g/N_k\) before any covariance calculation.
body.justification: This is the missing bridge from scalar block debiasing to one growing adoption-aligned event process.
body.gap: Choi and Yuan, Proposition A.4 and their staggered-adoption theorem, give block or scalar expansions but do not aggregate an increasing number of event horizons uniformly.
body.consumer: It supplies the vector score needed to attach whole-curve uncertainty to the Ben-Michael--Feller right-to-carry event plot.

obligation.what_is_open: A simultaneous heterogeneous-noise Choi--Yuan block expansion whose nonlinear errors satisfy \( |r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) for every eligible \( (g,k)\) on one event with probability tending to one uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\).
obligation.obstruction: The source-level Proposition A.4 in arXiv:2308.02364v1 is a one-block result under iid homoskedastic noise, with failure probability of order \(\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}\). The frozen class instead permits row heteroskedasticity and a growing collection of blocks. Even granting a heterogeneous extension block by block, the union-bound remainder is \(\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}\), which no frozen assumption forces to vanish. The definition of \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) names an upper-bound expression but is not a logical assertion that the estimator remainder obeys it.
obligation.attempted: Verified the exact primary-source Proposition A.4 and its probability statement, expanded the eligible-cohort aggregation before taking a maximum, and derived the precise sufficient simultaneous event and its direct union-bound probability. Neither a theorem-level heterogeneous adaptation nor the required block-count/tail relation is present in the frozen core.
obligation.partial_result:
For an eligible block \((g,k)\), define
\[
\widehat\tau_{gk}
=\frac{1}{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}
  \bigl(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}\bigr),
\qquad
\tau_{gk}=\frac{1}{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}\tau_{i,g+k},
\]
and let \(b_{gk,q}\) be the expression inside square brackets in the
definition of \(c_{kq}\).  Thus, by that definition,
\[
c_{kq}=\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}b_{gk,q}.
\]
If the exact block expansion is written as
\[
\widehat\tau_{gk}-\tau_{gk}
=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q+r_{gk},
\]
then the definitions of \(\widehat\tau_k\) and
\(\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\) give, by finite-sum rearrangement,
\[
\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q
 \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Since \(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\) and \(s_k>0\), the definition of
\(\rho_{n,k}\) therefore yields
\[
\rho_{n,k}
=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Consequently, on the simultaneous event
\[
\mathcal A_n(C)=
\bigcap_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\bigcap_{g\in E_k}
\bigl\{|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\bigr\},
\]
the triangle inequality and the definition of
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) imply the deterministic bound
\[
\|\rho_n\|_\infty
\le C\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
 \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}
=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
The verified one-block Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 gives, under its own
iid homoskedastic assumptions, a failure probability of order
\(\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}\).  Even if its conclusion were first
extended to the frozen heterogeneous model, a direct union bound would
only give
\[
P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
\le C'
\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
No frozen condition makes the last sum vanish.  Hence the exact vector
identity and the deterministic aggregation bound are proved, but the
claimed uniform stochastic order is not.
